lines.label: B1
lines.reason: This is the upper (flange-side) bend of the joggle, between the flange plate (patches 12/1) and the middle strip of the joggle (patches 11/15), about 24 deg. The convex (outer) skin is the patch-11/12 side. In 20 perpendicular sections from z=-75.7 to -8.2, the line sits on the outer-skin apex: median 0.06 mm, max 0.19 mm, about 0.18 mm from the sharp corner of the two plates. The fold exists only where the middle strip exists (z -76.4 to -7.5). The flange tab below z=-76.4 is a flat single plate (checked in sections at z=-80.3, -79 and -77.5). The line spans -76.44 to -7.52, so it covers 100% of the visible fold. It is parallel to the fold, with direction about +z.

lines.label: B2
lines.reason: This is the lower (arc-side) bend of the joggle, between patch 3, the flat tangent end of the rolled arc, and the middle strip (patch 15), about 18 deg. It bends against the arc's direction of curvature, so it is a real formed reverse fold and not part of the roll. The convex skin is the patch-3/15 side (+x). In 20 sections the line sits 0.23 to 0.39 mm (median 0.30 mm) from the rounded outer apex, under 1 mm, and the nearest skin point is 0.01 to 0.25 mm away. It runs the full extent of the strip, z -76.36 to -7.59, so coverage is 100%. It is parallel to the fold.
